name: Albany
note: Town: regional city and the region's main base, the oldest European settlement in WA, with the Torndirrup and Stirling Range gateway.

name: Denmark
note: Town: coastal town on Wilson Inlet, base for William Bay National Park, the Bibbulmun Track and the wineries.

name: Walpole
note: Town: small town at Nornalup Inlet, base for the Valley of the Giants and Walpole-Nornalup National Park.

name: Mount Barker
note: Town: service town and gateway to the Porongurup and Stirling Ranges, with a visitor centre in the old railway building.

name: Bremer Bay
note: Town: coastal town at the mouth of Bremer Bay, gateway to the east of Fitzgerald River NP.

name: Kojonup
note: Town: Albany Highway town with a 50 m outdoor pool and a golf club; a service stop, not a draw.

name: Katanning
note: Town: wheatbelt-edge town with a castle-like former winery building and sheep sculptures at its entrance.

name: Katanning All Ages Playground
note: Playground: unusual playground of oversized structures in Katanning, named in the town's Wikipedia article.

name: Albany Convict Gaol
note: Museum: restored 1852 convict gaol complex on Stirling Terrace, also the town's main museum.

name: Residency Museum
note: Museum: 1850s store later the Government Residency, with a white pointer jaw and the Eclipse Lighthouse lens.

name: Albany Wind Farm
note: Infrastructure viewpoint: 12 wind turbines at Sandpatch, 12 km south-west of the centre, with a car park and open access.

name: Brig Amity Replica
note: Museum ship: replica of the 1826 brig Amity that brought Albany's first settlers, boarded daily in the Historical Precinct.

name: Patrick Taylor Cottage
note: Museum: wattle-and-daub cottage built about 1832, the oldest surviving dwelling in Western Australia.

name: Princess Royal Fortress
note: Museum and fort: 1830s fortress site on the WWI convoy assembly point; the National ANZAC Centre is on this same site (the board listing "National ANZAC Centre" is attached here, not a second spot).

name: Albany Historic Whaling Station
note: Museum: former whaling station closed in 1978, with a self-guided tour and the Cheynes IV whale chaser.

name: Dog Rock
note: Landmark: granite rock that looks like a dog's head, beside Middleton Road near the supermarkets.

name: Old Post Office, Albany
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=viewpoint 'Old Albany Post Office, 1869'
note: Historic building: former customs and bond store on Stirling Terrace with a magnificent spiral tower stair, now housing restaurants and a museum.

name: Vancouver Arts Centre
note: Arts venue: former 1887 cottage hospital on Vancouver Street, a focal point for the arts; a venue rather than a sight.

name: Desert Mounted Corps War Memorial
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon historic=memorial 'Desert Mounted Corps Memorial'
note: War memorial: Port Said monument unveiled in 1932 on Albany's hill, with good views over the harbour.

name: Mount Clarence
note: Hill: walking trails around Mount Clarence from the war memorial, with views over Princess Royal Harbour and the town.

name: Mount Melville
note: Hill: summit with a sealed road, walk trails and an observation tower with panoramic views over Albany.

name: Quaranup Point Possession Trail
note: Walk: 1.6 km trail from the old Quarantine Station to Point Possession, where Vancouver claimed WA for Britain.

name: Albany Historic Town Trails
note: Walk: two self-guided heritage walks visiting 39 places within 2 km of the CBD, starting at the Gaol or Stirling Terrace.

name: Bibbulmun Track
note: Long trail: 963 km walking track from Kalamunda to Albany, passing Denmark, Walpole and West Cape Howe.

name: Munda Biddi Trail
note: Long trail: mountain-bike trail running from Mundaring to Albany through the jarrah, karri and tingle forests.

name: Albany Whale Tours
note: Operator: whale-watching and harbour cruises run from Shelley Beach Road; an operator, its place is the harbour and whales.

name: Middleton Beach
note: Beach: popular town beach closest to Albany's centre, with cafes and a relaxed promenade.

name: Frenchman Bay
note: Beach: sheltered beach beside Torndirrup National Park, reached by Frenchman Bay Road.

name: Ellen Cove
note: Beach: small cove at Middleton Beach, pictured in the Albany article.

name: Goode Beach
note: Beach: beach at the northern end of Goode Beach near Mistaken Island, Albany.

name: Muttonbird Island
note: Island and beach: island reserve with a beach among Albany's popular beaches.

name: Betty's Beach
note: Beach: sheltered beach near Albany, named after a family who camped there.

name: Nanarup Beach
note: Beach: white-sand beach on the Albany coast.

name: Cheynes Beach
note: Beach: beach at the site of the former Cheynes Beach Whaling Station south of Albany.

name: Misery Beach
note: Beach: beach about 20 km south of Albany on the Torndirrup coast, named for the whaling station's offal; DBCA-listed.

name: The Gap
note: Natural feature: granite inlet with clifftop platforms over the Southern Ocean, in Torndirrup National Park.

name: Natural Bridge
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=viewpoint 'Natural Bridge Lookout'
note: Natural feature: granite arch over the sea with a lookout platform, in Torndirrup National Park.

name: Blowholes
note: Natural feature: granite blowholes on the Torndirrup coast that spray with the swell.

name: Salmon Holes
note: Coastal lookout and fishing spot: rocky Torndirrup coast site named in DBCA's park gallery.

name: Cable Beach (Albany)
note: Beach: Torndirrup coast beach in DBCA's gallery; a different Cable Beach (Broome) is a separate place, so check the location.

name: Jimmy Newells
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon amenity=parking 'Jimmy Newells Inlet'
note: Natural feature: coastal harbour and boat launch on the Torndirrup coast, a DBCA-listed attraction.

name: Bald Head Walk Trail
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH (on trail, not verified as midpoint): photon highway=path 'Bald Head Trail'
note: Walk: up to 10 km return trail to Bald Head and Isthmus Hill, the longest walk in Torndirrup National Park.

name: Stony Hill Heritage Trail
note: Walk: short heritage trail in Torndirrup National Park, named in its Wikipedia article.

name: Torndirrup National Park
note: Park: coastal national park on the Torndirrup Peninsula with the Gap, Natural Bridge and Blowholes; the most-visited WA park.

name: HMAS Perth Wreck
note: Dive site: former cruiser sunk as a dive wreck in King George Sound in 2001.

name: Michaelmas Island
note: Island: island in King George Sound seen from Gull Rock lookouts; no visitor access per the sources.

name: Breaksea Island
note: Island: lighthouse island in King George Sound seen from Gull Rock National Park lookouts.

name: Bald Island
note: Island: island listed in the Great Southern islands category; access unclear.

name: Chatham Island
note: Island: small island off the Albany coast listed in the Great Southern islands category.

name: Eclipse Island
note: Island: lighthouse island off Albany, seen from the coast; not visitable.

name: Seal Island (Albany)
note: Island: small island in King George Sound listed in the Great Southern islands category.

name: Shelter Island
note: Island: island in the Great Southern islands category; access unclear.

name: Saddle Island
note: Island: island in the Great Southern islands category; access unclear.

name: Gould Island
note: Island: island in the Great Southern islands category; access unclear.

name: Green Island (Great Southern)
note: Island: island in the Great Southern islands category; access unclear.

name: Doubtful Islands
note: Island group: offshore group on the Great Southern coast; access unclear.

name: Gull Rock National Park
note: Park: 2,000 ha coastal park with high lookouts over King George Sound, Breaksea and Michaelmas islands and Ledge Beach.

name: Ledge Beach
note: Beach: sheltered white-sand beach in Gull Rock National Park, good for swimming and snorkelling.

name: Hassell National Park
note: Park: long narrow strip along South Coast Highway east of Albany; DBCA says it has no facilities or visitor sites.

name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: sheltered bay 35 km east of Albany with a visitor centre, Little Beach trails and noisy scrub-bird habitat.

name: Little Beach
note: Beach: sheltered sandy beach at Two Peoples Bay for swimming, diving and canoeing.

name: Sinker Reef Beach
note: Beach: 4WD-accessed beach on the Sinker Reef Track in the Two Peoples Bay reserve, with coastal views.

name: West Cape Howe National Park
note: Park: coastal park with granite and dolerite cliffs, the southernmost point of mainland WA and Bibbulmun Track access.

name: Shelley Beach
note: Beach: popular beach and campground in West Cape Howe NP with views to Torbay Head.

name: Shelley Beach Lookout
note: Lookout: clifftop lookout above Shelley Beach with platforms for hang gliding and paragliding; may overlap Shelley Beach.

name: Torbay Head
note: Headland: rugged granite headland in view from Shelley Beach and the West Cape Howe coastline.

name: Dunsky Beach
note: Beach: beach in West Cape Howe National Park, named in DBCA's gallery.

name: Waterfall Beach
note: Beach: beach at Two Peoples Bay, named in the Albany article.

name: Fitzgerald River National Park
note: Park: whole Fitzgerald River NP, a large coastal park with 75 plant species found nowhere else and whale-watching.

name: Point Ann
note: Viewpoint: whale-watching platform on Point Ann where southern right whales calve June to October.

name: Whalebone Beach
note: Beach: beach in Fitzgerald River NP, the park's first-listed gallery beach.

name: West Mount Barren
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'West Mount Barren'
note: Peak: highest point of the Barren Range (372 m), with a 2-hour return walk to the top and wide views.

name: Barren Range
note: Range: coastal range along the length of Fitzgerald River NP with West, Mid and East Mt Barren; overlaps West Mount Barren.

name: Quoin Head
note: Headland: coastal headland with a campground in Fitzgerald River NP, a DBCA gallery stop.

name: St Mary Inlet
note: Inlet: inlet and campground in Fitzgerald River NP for swimming, boating and fishing.

name: Hamersley Inlet
note: Inlet: estuary inlet in Fitzgerald River NP for boating and fishing.

name: Hellfire Bay
note: Bay: sheltered bay in Fitzgerald River NP for swimming and snorkelling.

name: Hakea Trail
note: Walk: bushwalk trail in Fitzgerald River NP for the park's plant diversity, named in DBCA's gallery.

name: Hamersley Drive
note: Drive: scenic road through Fitzgerald River NP, named in DBCA's gallery.

name: Mount Hassell
note: Peak: DBCA-listed peak; location within the region to be checked.

name: Dillon Bay
note: Beach: beach just east of Bremer Bay, a recreational beach-fishing spot.

name: Denmark Historical Museum
note: Museum: local history museum on Mitchell Street about Denmark's timber and industrial past.

name: William Bay National Park
note: Park: windswept granite headlands and sheltered bays 14 km west of Denmark, home to Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks.

name: Greens Pool
note: Beach: sheltered swimming pool ringed by granite boulders in William Bay NP, a main summer draw.

name: Elephant Rocks
note: Beach and rock formation: granite boulders that look like wading elephants, a 10-minute walk from Greens Pool.

name: Ocean Beach
note: Beach: patrolled tourist beach about 5 km south of Denmark at Ratcliffe Bay, with a lifeguard in summer.

name: Denmark Wineries
note: Wine region: group of cool-climate wineries and cellar doors around Denmark (a grouping, not one place).

name: Mount Frankland National Park
note: Park: granite peak with a fire lookout, walking trails and car park; boundary is near the South West / Great Southern line.

name: Walpole-Nornalup National Park
note: Park: tingle and karri forest and inlets around Walpole, with the Valley of the Giants and Giants Trails.

name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
wiki: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
note: Walk: 600 m treetop walkway 40 m above the ancient tingle forest.

name: Giant Tingle Tree
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: OSM tourism=attraction 'Giant Tingle Tree'
note: Tree: giant red tingle tree reached by an 800 m circular walk from the car park beyond Hilltop Lookout.

name: Hilltop Lookout
note: Lookout: forest-clearing lookout over the Frankland River, Nornalup Inlet and the ocean, first stop on Hill Top Scenic Drive.

name: Circular Pool
note: Pool: viewing platforms over the Frankland River's circular pool in Walpole-Nornalup NP.

name: Coalmine Beach
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: OSM amenity=parking 'Coalmine Beach Car Park'
note: Beach: family swimming and paddling beach on the north shore of Nornalup Inlet, with picnic area and holiday park.

name: Irwin Inlet
note: Inlet: Walpole-Nornalup inlet for swimming, paddling and fishing; DBCA-listed.

name: Mount Clare
note: Lookout: summit and viewpoint in the Walpole Wilderness, reached by walk and drive; DBCA-listed.

name: Conspicuous Beach
note: Beach: remote beach in the Walpole-Nornalup area named in local visitor listings.

name: Porongurup National Park
note: Park: granite Porongurup Range with the Granite Skywalk, scenic drives and walking tracks.

name: Granite Skywalk
note: Walk: 4.4 km return trail to a Castle Rock lookout with a suspended skywalk section.

name: Castle Rock
note: Lookout: granite peak with views north to the Stirling Range and south to the coast, reached by the Granite Skywalk.

name: Devils Slide
note: Rock feature: granite formation in Porongurup National Park, named in DBCA's gallery.

name: Gibraltar Rock
note: Rock: granite outcrop in the Porongurup Range, pictured in the Porongurup article.

name: Castle Rock Estate
note: Winery: cellar door at the foot of the Porongurup Range with views of the Stirling Range; a venue, not a sight.

name: Stirling Range National Park
note: Park: the only major mountain range in the south of WA, with peaks over 1,000 m, wildflower walks and drives.

name: Bluff Knoll
note: Peak: highest peak in southern WA (1,099 m) with a summit walk and eastern lookout.

name: Mount Trio
note: Peak: Stirling Range peak with walking tracks, on the northern boundary near Mount Trio bush camp.

name: Toolbrunup Peak
note: Peak: Stirling Range summit with a walking track, DBCA gallery.

name: Stirling Range Scenic Drive
note: Drive: 42 km mostly unsealed graded scenic drive through the Stirling Range NP.

name: Cape Riche
note: Headland: coastal cape on the south coast east of Albany with a Wikipedia article; a visitor draw is not sourced.

name: Puntapin Rock
note: Rock: granite outcrop (peak) in the Great Southern wheatbelt edge; no visitor source found.

name: Oyster Harbour
note: Waterway: inlet at Albany's north-east, a water body rather than a place to go.

name: King George Sound
note: Waterway: the sound that Albany sits on, seen from the Gull Rock and Torndirrup lookouts; a body of water.

name: Albany Town Hall
note: Civic building: 1887 town hall on York Street with a theatre; seen from the street.

name: Valley of the Giants
note: Valley of the Giants forest and tingle-tree area, a visitor site in Walpole-Nornalup NP with the Tree Top Walk.

name: The Kodja Place
note: Cultural centre: Aboriginal cultural centre in Albany run with the Menang people, a visitor venue.

name: Museum of the Great Southern
note: Museum: regional museum of the Great Southern (location in the region to be checked).

name: Honeymoon Pool
note: Swimming pool: natural pool listed by the regional board (location in the region to be checked).

name: Denmark Animal Farm and Pentland Alpaca Stud
note: Farm attraction: animal farm and alpaca stud near Denmark, a private visitor farm (an operator, not a natural place).

name: Denmark Chocolate Company
note: Shop: chocolate maker and shop in Denmark; a business, not a sight.

name: Albany Tours
note: Operator: tour company in Albany; an operator, not a place.

name: Kaarl Wirn Cultural Tours Albany
note: Operator: Aboriginal cultural tours in Albany; an operator, not a place.

name: WOW Wilderness EcoCruise
note: Operator: eco cruise on the Walpole inlets; an operator, its place is the inlet.

name: Whale Watch Western Australia
note: Operator: whale-watching tours (location in the region to be checked); an operator, its place is the whales and coast.

name: Mount Trio Bush Camp and Caravan Park
note: Accommodation: bush camp and caravan park at the Stirling Range; accommodation, not a spot.

name: Cheynes Beach Caravan Park
note: Accommodation: caravan park beside Cheynes Beach; accommodation, not a spot.

name: The Lake House Denmark
note: Accommodation and restaurant in Denmark; a business, not a spot.

name: Fernhook Falls
note: Waterfall and pool: Deep River falls and Rowell's Pool in Mount Frankland South NP, with boardwalks and a campground; DBCA-listed.

name: East Mount Barren
note: Peak: quartzite peak on the eastern edge of Fitzgerald River NP, a hard summit walk with views; DBCA-listed.

name: Lights Beach
note: Beach: beach just east of William Bay NP on the Bibbulmun Track, for surfing, fishing and walking; DBCA-listed.

name: Mandalay Beach
note: Beach: wide beach between Manjimup and Walpole, DBCA-listed; the Mandalay wreck can be seen at low tide (part of this beach, not a separate spot). Boundary: D'Entrecasteaux NP, west of Walpole, so South West per the region notes.

name: Emu Point
note: Village and beach: Emu Point on King George Sound with a 2.9 km beach and a holiday park; Wikipedia only.

name: Peaceful Bay
note: Village: small village partly surrounded by Walpole-Nornalup NP with a chalet development; Wikipedia only.

name: Mount Romance Sandalwood Factory
note: Venue: sandalwood factory near Albany with daily information tours and a shop; a commercial venue, not a natural place.

name: Plantagenet Wines
note: Winery: cellar door and café at Mount Barker, the region's first winery (1975); a venue with tastings.

name: Mount Barker Wineries
note: Wine region: grouping of the Mount Barker sub-region's wineries and cellar doors (not one place).

name: Bornholm
note: Locality: coastal locality between Albany and Denmark covered by West Cape Howe NP; no visitor site named.

name: Wilson Inlet
note: Inlet: estuary beside Denmark, breached at Ocean Beach; a water body rather than a place to go.
